description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%p-maybe-autoflush` (~line 4084): `(and (plusp (hash-table-count *p-autoflush-handles*)) (gethash stream *p-autoflush-handles*))`.  The count guard keeps programs that never set `$|` free; one `$| = 1` (STDOUT -- an everyday idiom) makes the count 1 for the rest of the run, and from then on every print to every handle pays a gethash on a :weakness :key table, which in SBCL takes the global system lock (the #4061 / #4501 / #4525 family).

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/rp/fprint0.pl vs afprint.pl: 1 M `print $fh "x\n"` to /dev/null, the second with `$| = 1;` on STDOUT -- $fh itself is NOT autoflushed, so the only difference is the probe; ab.pl --emit, best of 7, legs/leg2.log, load 1.3): 0.074 -> 0.134 s whole run, +81.1 % (C/A -3.1 %).  ~60 ns per print.

THE FIX (runtime only): keep the autoflush mark where a probe is free -- e.g. a short simple-vector of the (at most a few) autoflushed streams compared with EQ, the stream dropped from it at close and at `$| = 0`; or a slot/plist mark on PCL's own stream wrapper if there is one.  The weak table exists so an abandoned handle is not pinned: removal at close (and at the handle's scope exit, #2006(b)) covers that; a handle abandoned WITHOUT close stays in a vector of a few entries, which is bounded by the number of handles a program ever set `$|` on.

BAR: the autoflush guard rows (grep -l 'autoflush\|\$|' Pl/t), io companion one-file runs (io/print.t-family), the measurement above reproduced (expect afprint ~= fprint0), gate.

DO NOT: drop the count guard -- programs without `$|` must stay at zero cost; do not flush on every print.

=== s540 (2026-11-13) === scheduled: s540/s540d-prompt.md (the USER: the speed fixing is a normal task).


=== DONE (s540d) ===
BUILT (runtime only).  *p-autoflush-handles* stays the authority (weak keys, so an abandoned handle is not pinned); a print now reads it through %p-maybe-autoflush's inline one-fixnum count test when nothing is marked (as on the base; a fix-forward, the s540d commit "#4983 fix-forward": with the %p-autoflush-p call ahead of that test the full bench read fhprint 3-6 % slower than the base), then %p-autoflush-p, else a scan of **p-autoflush-mirror** -- a simple-vector of at most 8 WEAK POINTERS compared with EQ, lock-free (a weak hash table is a synchronized one in SBCL: ~57 ns a GETHASH).  The mirror is re-taken when the table's count differs from the one it was taken at (a writer through %p-autoflush-mark drops it; a direct table write -- cl/pcl-test.lisp's TAP stream -- or an entry the collector dropped moves the count); more than 8 marked handles = the table answers.  The setter, the getter, p-local-pipe and %p-carry-autoflush go through %p-autoflush-mark.  MEASURED (bench1, quiet, best of 5): 1 M prints after `$| = 1` 0.137 -> 0.076 s (-44.0 %, band 0.7 %); on the tree the same loop without `$|` takes 0.074 s (+3.1 % against a band of 3.0 %: back to the no-`$|` time).  On the FINAL runtime (after the #4983 fix-forward, legs/bench5.log): 1 M prints with `$| = 1` 0.144 -> 0.077 s (-46.9 %, band 0.1) and without 0.072 -> 0.072 s (+0.3 %, band 0.5: the base), against 75904a35, whole runs best of 7 (legs/bench5.log); bench-exec K=9 fhprint +2.4 % and fprint +2.3 % (bands +0.5 / -0.1).  The other per-print reads, named and NOT changed: the tied-handle table (**p-handle-tie-table**, the same count-guarded weak shape once ANY handle is tied: on the tree 1 M prints to an UNTIED handle take 0.198 s once another handle is tied against 0.075 s with none tied (+165 %, ~120 ns a print) -- filed #5023), the signal-hold binding once any %SIG handler exists (a special binding + unwind-protect, no table), $, and $\ (plain boxes).  Guards: Pl/t/perf-levers-16.t rows 4-5 (mirror / direct write / more than 8 / cleared; fail on the base) + row 7 (perl's output: per selected handle, local, ten handles, -s after a flushed write, the clamp).  Companion io/print.t 23/1, io/say.t 13/0, op/select.t 3/6 = the snapshot.  s540c (handle lifetime) does not touch the autoflush code; its finalizer closes collected streams, which the mirror's weak pointers and count check absorb.
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): once ANY handle has `$|` set (`$| = 1;` at the top of a script), EVERY print to ANY handle probes the WEAK table *p-autoflush-handles* (SBCL's global lock) -- 1 M prints to a file +81 % (0.074 -> 0.134 s); a #4061 sibling
